transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m convinced that a former client has quietly used my proprietary strategic frameworks to structure their policies in a way that intentionally pushes me out of my own field, and I simply cannot be talked out of this belief. I am here today at the suggestion of a younger colleague I mentor, who felt my persistent focus on this situation warranted a professional evaluation.
Besides this specific belief about your former client, have you experienced any other unusual sensations, such as hearing voices that others cannot hear or seeing things that aren't there?

No, I have never experienced anything like that at all. My senses are completely normal, and I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. Aside from my concerns about this former client, my mind is perfectly clear.
Have you ever had any significant head injuries, seizures, or diagnosed medical conditions that affect your brain, such as tumors or neurological disorders?
No, I have never experienced any head injuries, seizures, or other neurological conditions. My medical history is entirely clear of any brain-related issues or physical trauma.
Has this belief about your former client caused you to experience significant problems in your daily life, such as issues with your job performance or your relationships with others?

In my day-to-day life, everything is completely normal—I manage my household, keep up with my painting, and maintain my daily routines without any issues. However, it has impacted my work because I've turned down several collaborations and referrals from anyone associated with that client's network, believing they are part of the effort to edge me out. This has unfortunately restricted my consulting opportunities much more than I ever intended with my semi-retirement.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to organize your thoughts, or have others mentioned that your speech or behavior seems disorganized or difficult to follow?

No, not at all; my mind feels completely clear and focused. Those who don't know about my situation with the client still see me as my usual, highly organized self. I continue to manage my household, daily routines, painting, and workshops without any trouble whatsoever.
How long have you held this specific belief about your former client, and did it begin after a specific event or interaction?
I’ve held this conviction for about eleven months now. It began shortly after I wrapped up a major advisory contract with that specific client and started transitioning into semi-retirement.
